finding: Timed window in one row: period and length in minutes from a start date, capped by an end date; the server computes the next toggle once per check (GameEventMgr.cpp, NextCheck).

Progress event: each linked quest adds to a counter; when every counter reaches its required number the event waits a set number of minutes and then starts the follow-up event. No timeout on the progress path.
Six-state machine per event (normal, inactive, conditions, next phase, finished, internal), saved per event so a restart keeps progress; a world-state flag and a bar are pushed to each player.

Holiday ritual: at minute zero of the hour a cheer and a burst fire, then a burst every one to two seconds at a random spot from a per-zone list until minute ten; a New Year finale at 00:10:30 with ten bursts.

Zalazane's Fall chain: a tiger vehicle within fifteen yards summons the matriarch for its summoner (checked every five seconds, blocked by a fifty-second no-summon aura); below twenty percent health she becomes non-attackable and summons the next boss.
Announce is one byte per event (silent, announce, or follow config): a server-wide chat line on start. Event content rows are not in the donor box; only the schema (14 game_event tables) is present.
Code is GPL-2.0; category-level inspiration only (window formula, progress gate, per-summoner lock, staged switch). No code, table or content copied.

Battlefield match with phases: queue fills to corps size times two, a 20-second start countdown, timed play, victory on score, then a result wait before teardown; the score line carries the scorer's name live.
Queue start threshold and the 60-second expiry are not settled: the expiry is only a TODO, and the start rule's queue-count meaning was not settled in the half read.
Roaming big monster: wanders within a six-unit square of its post, pauses three to five seconds between hops, switches to attack on aggro; group-member handling is a TODO.
Cron-gated spawners and doodads: four schedule tables (day of week, clock window, start and end dates) decide when a camp or prop is present; the rows live in a SQLite game-data file not in the repo.
Two battlefield records in data (ids 11 and 7), each with a Corps1 and Corps2 spawn point; no invasion or world-boss timer found in the matching lines read.
Code licence conflicts in the repo (LGPL v3 README, GPL v3 and MIT files); no code copied; data carries no licence line.
